Option A '5 patients' is exactly the VARIANCE, not the S.D. — the stem asks for standard deviation, so the only defensible reading is that the key intends A via a variance/S.D. confusion.
Range = largest - smallest = (-4) - (-44) = 40. Range is a non-negative spread, so the signed options -48 and -40 are distractors; 40 exactly.
C.V. = (S.D. / mean) x 100 by definition, which is precisely the described quantity; the coefficient of S.D. is the same ratio WITHOUT the x100 percentage.

S.D. of first n natural numbers = sqrt((n^2 - 1)/12) = sqrt(2) gives (n^2 - 1)/12 = 2, n^2 = 25, n = 5. Checked all options: n=4 -> sqrt(5/4)=1.118, n=6 -> 1.708, n=7 -> 2 exactly; only n=5 yields sqrt(2)=1.4142.
Mean of the squared deviations from the mean IS the variance; its positive square root is the standard deviation. The 'positive square root of' clause is what makes it S.D. rather than option A.

The second set is the first shifted by a constant -5 (19-5=14, 21-5=16, ...), and variance is invariant under a shift of origin. Computed directly: mean 18, deviations -4,-2,0,2,4, squares sum 40, variance 40/5 = 8 — identical to the first set's 8.

For two numbers a, b: mean = (a+b)/2, both deviations are +/-(a-b)/2, so variance = (a-b)^2/4 and S.D. = |a-b|/2 = range/2. Verified numerically on three random pairs. NOTE this depends on the population divisor n=2 (the book's convention); with the sample divisor n-1=1 the S.D. would be |a-b|/sqrt(2) = 0.707 x range, matching no option — so B is correct only under the population convention this chapter uses.
